_comment: In-process HTTP test client fidelity. Feature 131, TC-DEC-01/02.
The TestClient is the middle path between a real socket (slow, flaky) and
calling a handler function directly (skips routing/middleware/the auth
gate/sessions). Its whole value is fidelity: client.get(...) must hit
exactly what a real GET hits, or the test proves nothing about production.
Python (core.server.app), PHP (Router::dispatch) and Ruby (RackApp#call)
have always routed a TestClient request through the REAL front controller.
Node's TestClient did not -- it RE-IMPLEMENTED the dispatch order instead
of calling the server's own dispatch stage-walker (TC-NODE-REIMPL), and
skipped stages the live server runs: (a) the SESSION stage never ran, so
the auth gate's session-token path was STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE through
TestClient -- a session-auth regression could never be caught; (b) the
gate-vs-route-middleware order was INVERTED (route middleware before the
gate; the live order is gate-before-middleware, ADR-0012), so a request
the live server would already have 401'd still ran the route's own
middleware; (c) the global-middleware pre/post-match partition,
template-route rendering, and static/landing fallbacks were not
reproduced. See tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/131-test-client.md.
The fix (TC-DEC-01) makes Node's TestClient call the SAME function every
live socket connection runs: packages/core/src/server.ts now exports
runDispatch(ctx, rawReq, rawRes) -- the dispatch closure that used to be
trapped inside startServer(), now parametrised by an explicit
DispatchContext (router/middleware/filesystem roots/Frond) instead of
closing over startServer()'s locals, so it can be driven from two places:
the live socket server (the FULL context, wired to real ORM/Swagger/
DevAdmin/CSRF registrations) and the in-process TestClient
(buildDispatchContext(), when no live server is running in this process,
or getLiveDispatchContext() when one is -- preferring the live one for
maximum fidelity, mirroring Ruby's RackApp.current). TestClient's own
hand-rolled matching/middleware/auth/fallback logic is DELETED, not
reimplemented on top -- maintainability = less code. A real correctness
consequence of fixing the order: a route middleware that used to run on a
would-be-401 request no longer does (documented as a breaking change, not
a bug in this fixture).
TC-DEC-02: TestResponse collapsed a duplicate response header (two
Set-Cookie) to the LAST value on read -- Python's ASGI header LIST was
flattened straight into a dict; PHP's TestResponse read ONLY
Response::getHeaders() (cookies live in a SEPARATE store, precisely so
more than one survives, and getHeaders() never included them at all -- a
real gap, not a collapse). Fixed in all four by keeping every value in
emission order and adding a multi accessor (get_all / getList /
getHeaderList) alongside the unchanged back-compat single (last-value)
accessor.
Fixing this exposed two adjacent, PRE-EXISTING defects the audit had not
named, found empirically while proving the session-login case for real
(not scope-creep -- both are required for TC-DEC-01/02 to hold at all):
* PHP: the session-cookie WRITE side branched on PHP's headers_sent(),
which a CLI process (TestClient, PHPUnit) never flips true, so the
session cookie was emitted via native setcookie() into a void nothing
ever reads back. Response gained isTesting() (backed by the EXISTING
constructor flag no caller had opted into for TestClient); Router's
emitSessionCookie() now also checks it. The session-cookie READ side
separately read PHP's raw $_COOKIE superglobal directly -- populated
only by a real HTTP SAPI -- instead of the abstracted
$request->cookies Request::create() already parses from the SAME
Cookie header; fixed to prefer $request->cookies, falling back to
$_COOKIE. (A live Tina4\Server instance was confirmed, empirically,
to ALSO never emit a first-time session cookie, for the identical
headers_sent() reason -- tracked separately, out of scope here.)
* Node: sessionAutoStart wrote the session Set-Cookie via
rawRes.setHeader(...), which REPLACES any Set-Cookie a route handler
had already set via response.cookie() -- live server included, not
just TestClient. Fixed to rawRes.appendHeader(...), which adds to an
existing value (or behaves exactly like setHeader when nothing is set
yet).
Four cases, the SAME names in each language's own idiom, driving the REAL
in-process dispatch with NO mocks:
* test_client_response_equals_a_real_socket_request -- THE ORACLE
(ported from Ruby's tina4-ruby spec/test_client_pipeline_spec.rb, the
model for this fixture). Boots a REAL server on a real socket, drives
the SAME route both ways, asserts status/body/content-type/a custom
marker header are byte-identical. Node's oracle route additionally
touches req.session so the oracle alone catches a reintroduced skip
of Node's specific historical gap, not just a generic mismatch.
* a_secured_route_returns_401_without_running_its_route_middleware --
a secured route with an ATTACHED route middleware that flips a
visible marker; a tokenless request 401s AND the marker stays unset
(gate-before-middleware, ADR-0012), then a valid-token positive
control proves the marker mechanism itself works.
* a_session_login_then_authenticated_request_succeeds -- a public
login route sets request.session (token), the Set-Cookie is threaded
BY HAND (no cookie jar -- TC-NO-COOKIE-JAR stays deliberately out of
scope) into a second request to a session-guarded route; a no-cookie
negative control precedes it.
* duplicate_response_headers_are_all_exposed -- a route calling
response.cookie() twice; the multi accessor returns both, the single
accessor keeps collapsing to the last (back-compat). The framework
auto-starts a session on every request independent of the route
under test, so a third, incidental Set-Cookie is real and expected
-- each suite filters to the two cookies the route set on purpose
rather than asserting a bare count.
Mutation-proved: (Node) restoring the re-implemented dispatch turns the
oracle, gate-order and session-login cases red (a session/middleware
TypeError or the inverted marker, depending on the case) -- restored
green. (Python/PHP/Ruby) restoring a last-wins/no-cookie header read
turns duplicate_response_headers_are_all_exposed red -- restored green.
Reap every socket/server/port/temp app opened; positive AND negative
assertions throughout.

invariants.rule: TestClient dispatches a request through the SAME real front controller the live server runs -- Python core.server.app, PHP Router::dispatch, Ruby RackApp#call, and now Node server.ts's exported runDispatch(ctx, ...) via a DispatchContext (the live server's own context when one is running in this process, else a standalone one bound to the given/default router) -- never a parallel re-implementation. No stage is skipped: the session stage attaches request.session before any route matching, the auth gate runs BEFORE the route's own middleware (ADR-0012), and global middleware, template-route rendering, and static/landing fallbacks all come free because the client shares the real stage-walker instead of reproducing it.
invariants.why: Node's TestClient re-implemented dispatch (TC-NODE-REIMPL): the session stage never ran, so a session-token auth regression was structurally unreachable through TestClient, and route middleware ran BEFORE the gate (inverted from live). A green Node TestClient test could hide a live session-auth failure or a middleware that processes a request the live server would already have rejected. Fixed by deleting the parallel dispatch and calling the real one -- maintainability = less code, not more. Mutation-proved: reverting Node's TestClient to the re-implemented dispatch turns the oracle (a session-touching route throws / diverges from the live socket), the gate-order case (the marker fires before the 401), and the session-login case (request.session is undefined) all red.
cases: test client response equals a real socket request
a secured route returns 401 without running its route middleware
a session login then authenticated request succeeds

invariants.rule: TestResponse preserves EVERY value of a duplicate response header (e.g. two Set-Cookie from two response.cookie() calls), in emission order, via a multi accessor (Python get_all(name), PHP getList(name), Ruby get_all(name), Node getHeaderList(name)). The existing single-value accessor (headers[name] / headers.get(name)) is UNCHANGED back-compat shape: it keeps collapsing to the LAST value, so no existing reader breaks.
invariants.why: Python's TestResponse collapsed the ASGI header LIST into a last-wins DICT at construction, so a second Set-Cookie silently overwrote the first -- a test could not assert on more than one. PHP's TestResponse read ONLY Response::getHeaders() (a plain scalar map); cookies live in a SEPARATE store keyed by cookie name specifically so more than one survives, and getHeaders() never included them -- a real gap, not merely a collapse, confirmed empirically: PHP's TestClient could not see a Set-Cookie AT ALL before this fix. Ruby's Response#to_rack already folds a repeated Set-Cookie into one '\n'-joined hash value (the Rack convention), so TestResponse needed to split it back into a list. Node's TestResponse already received a real array from ServerResponse.getHeaders() for a multi-value header but collapsed it with .join(', ') -- unsafe specifically for Set-Cookie, whose own Expires attribute can itself contain a comma. Mutation-proved: (Python) reverting to the last-wins dict, (Ruby) reverting to a single collapsed value, (PHP) reverting the cookie merge, and (Node) reverting to the old TestClient (whose TestResponse never had a multi accessor at all) each turn duplicate_response_headers_are_all_exposed red.
cases: duplicate response headers are all exposed
